summary: Carlos I (1863–1908) was king of Portugal from 1889. His reign opened with the British Ultimatum of 1890, which forced Portugal out of the territory between Angola and Mozambique and cost the crown much of its standing. It ran on through two declarations of bankruptcy and the slow exhaustion of the rotation of parties. In 1906 he called João Franco to govern. In 1907 he consented to Franco dissolving parliament and ruling by decree. The crown became a party to the dictatorship, and it stopped being an arbiter above the parties. Gunmen shot him and his heir dead in Lisbon on 1 February 1908. He is in the atlas as the last Portuguese king who governed as well as reigned.
